answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with quadratic staking: each identity's influence is the square root of its locked stake. An honest agent staking 100 units wields influence 10. A sybil splitting that same 100 across many fakes, scattering seeds across a meadow, gains only sqrt(100*N) influence, sublinear growth that shrinks per copy. Each fake must be funded and kept alive, so marginal cost climbs while reward falls. Honest work compounds like a crystal on one nucleus; the stake pool becomes a tended garden where whole roots yield and scattered seeds sprout only weeds.
